intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local street vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently using a street food map.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, browse the vibrant night market, release a lantern on the Thu Bon River, and taste local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from street stalls. The town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns every evening, creating a magical cultural atmosphere.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass between Da Nang and Hue, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic coastal mountain roads. Stop at the old French and American war bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of the South China Sea and lush green mountains.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat Tour & Local Village Homestay
experiences.description: Take a budget boat tour through the waterways of the Mekong Delta, visiting floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and rice paper factories. Interact with local farmers, sample tropical fruits, and optionally stay overnight in a family-run homestay for an authentic rural Vietnamese cultural experience.

experiences.name: Banh Mi & Pho Cooking Class in Hue
experiences.description: Join an affordable hands-on cooking class in Vietnam's imperial city of Hue, learning to prepare traditional Central Vietnamese dishes including Bun Bo Hue, Banh Khoai (crispy pancakes), and fresh spring rolls. Classes typically include a local market visit to source ingredients and a sit-down meal of everything you cook.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.date: Day 1 – April 15 (Arrival Day)
day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly public bus No. 17 or 86 to the Old Quarter (around 9,000–45,000 VND). Check into your boutique hostel/guesthouse in the Old Quarter. Freshen up and take a slow orientation walk through the iconic 36 ancient streets of the Old Quarter – explore Hang Gai, Hang Bac, and Hang Dao streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the evening atmosphere – watch locals exercise, play chess, and socialize around the lake. Cross the red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (entry ~30,000 VND). Stroll Ta Hien Street (Beer Street) for cheap Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and soak in the backpacker vibe.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi from a street stall near the Old Quarter after check-in (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at a local street pho stall on Bat Dan Street – one of Hanoi's most famous pho spots (~50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local bank/gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Avoid airport taxi touts – use Grab app or official bus for safe, cheap transport. SIM cards available at the airport for ~150,000–200,000 VND.

day_by_day.date: Day 2 – April 16 (Hanoi Culture Day)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00–7:00 AM) to witness the morning street food scene. Visit Dong Xuan Market, Hanoi's oldest and largest covered market, for a cultural immersion. Then head to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex – see the mausoleum exterior, One Pillar Pagoda, and Ho Chi Minh Museum (entry ~40,000 VND). Arrive early as the mausoleum has limited visiting hours (typically 7:30–10:30 AM, closed Mon/Fri).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first national university, a stunning Confucian temple complex (~30,000 VND entry). Spend 1–2 hours exploring the courtyards and learning about Vietnamese scholarly history. Afterward, visit the nearby Fine Arts Museum of Vietnam (~40,000 VND) to see traditional lacquerware, silk paintings, and sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter and watch the Hoan Kiem Lake area transform at dusk. Visit the famous Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre for a traditional water puppet show (~100,000 VND – book in advance). This is a uniquely Vietnamese art form not to be missed.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street vendor near the hotel (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Cha (grilled pork with rice noodles) at a local eatery near the Temple of Literature (~50,000–70,000 VND) – the dish made famous by Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama
meals.dinner: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a street stall in the Old Quarter (~40,000–60,000 VND), followed by Che (sweet dessert soup) for ~15,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and during October–November for annual maintenance. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for temple visits. Bargain politely at Dong Xuan Market.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~70,000–100,000 VND). Alternatively, book a budget day tour from the Old Quarter (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport). On arrival, rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle through the stunning Tam Coc valley – known as 'Ha Long Bay on land.' Take a 2-hour rowboat ride through three cave tunnels past dramatic limestone karsts and rice paddies (~150,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free entry), a beautiful pagoda built into a limestone cave. Continue to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (~20,000 VND entry) – the 10th-century capital of Vietnam with ancient temples dedicated to the Dinh and Le dynasties. Climb the nearby viewpoint for panoramic rice paddy and karst views.
day_by_day.evening: Return bus to Hanoi. Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 7:00–8:00 PM. Decompress with a Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Trung – egg coffee, ~45,000 VND) at a rooftop café overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near your hostel before departure (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or fresh spring rolls at a local restaurant in Tam Coc village (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) at a street stall in the Old Quarter upon return (~50,000–65,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Start early to avoid midday heat and crowds at Tam Coc. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Goat cheese is a local Ninh Binh specialty – try it if available. The rowboat is paddled by local women, often with their feet – tipping is appreciated (~20,000–50,000 VND).

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – April 18 (Travel to Hue via Sleeper Bus)
day_by_day.morning: Spend your last morning in Hanoi exploring any missed spots in the Old Quarter. Visit the Hanoi Old Quarter Walking Street (pedestrian zone on weekends) or browse the antique shops on Hang Bong Street. Pack your bags and check out of the hostel (arrange luggage storage if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanoi's Giap Bat or My Dinh bus station and board an overnight sleeper bus to Hue (~200,000–350,000 VND, approximately 12–14 hours). Buses typically depart between 6:00–9:00 PM. Spend the afternoon relaxing, visiting a local café, or doing laundry before your overnight journey.
day_by_day.evening: Board the overnight sleeper bus to Hue. These Vietnamese sleeper buses have reclining seats/pods and are a quintessential backpacking experience. Sleep as the bus winds through the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Chao (rice porridge) at a local breakfast spot near the hostel (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local eatery (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Grab food from a street market or convenience store before boarding the bus (~30,000–50,000 VND) – stock up on snacks for the overnight journey

day_by_day.notes: Book the sleeper bus in advance through your hostel or platforms like Baolau or 12Go Asia. Choose reputable companies like Phuong Trang (FUTA) or The Sinh Tourist. Keep valuables in your day bag, not in the overhead compartment. The bus passes through the spectacular Hai Van Pass.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19 (Hue – Imperial City)
day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Hue early morning (~6:00–8:00 AM). Check into a budget guesthouse in the city center (~150,000–250,000 VND/night). Freshen up and head to the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Dai Noi) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty (~200,000 VND entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the vast walled complex, including the Forbidden Purple City, Thai Hoa Palace, and ornate gates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND) or hire a xe om (motorbike taxi) to visit the Royal Tombs along the Perfume River. Visit the dramatic Tomb of Khai Dinh (~150,000 VND) – a striking blend of Vietnamese and European baroque architecture – and the serene Tomb of Minh Mang (~150,000 VND), set among lakes and pine forests.
day_by_day.evening: Take a walk along the Perfume River at sunset. Visit Dong Ba Market for local handicrafts and street food. Explore the vibrant Pham Ngu Lao backpacker street for cheap eats and cold beer.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Hue or Com Hen (baby clam rice) – a Hue breakfast specialty (~30,000–50,000 VND) near the market
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant – this is the dish's birthplace (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Khoai (Hue sizzling crepes) and Nem Lui (lemongrass pork skewers) at a street food stall near Dong Ba Market (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hue's cuisine is considered the most refined in Vietnam – try as many local specialties as possible. A combo ticket for multiple royal tombs can save money. Hue can be rainy – pack a light rain jacket. The city is very bicycle-friendly.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20 (Hue to Hoi An via Hai Van Pass)
day_by_day.morning: Hire a motorbike (self-drive ~100,000–150,000 VND/day) or join a budget group tour (~200,000–350,000 VND) for the iconic coastal drive over Hai Van Pass – one of Vietnam's most scenic mountain roads with breathtaking ocean views. Stop at the top for panoramic photos. Continue to Lang Co Beach for a quick swim and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Da Nang (~1 hour from Hue). Optional quick stop at the Marble Mountains (~40,000 VND) – a cluster of five marble and limestone hills with caves, tunnels, and Buddhist sanctuaries. Continue the 30km drive south to Hoi An. Check into a budget hostel in or near the Ancient Town (~150,000–250,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.evening: Take a magical first evening stroll through Hoi An Ancient Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its lantern-lit streets. Buy a lantern (~20,000–50,000 VND) and release it on the Thu Bon River for good luck (~20,000 VND). Explore the narrow streets glowing with hundreds of silk lanterns.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or sticky rice from a street vendor before departure (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local restaurant in Lang Co or Da Nang (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature noodle dish, made with water from a specific ancient well) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~70,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass drive is one of the most iconic experiences in Vietnam – featured on Top Gear. If self-driving a motorbike, ensure you are licensed and confident. Alternatively, the train from Hue to Da Nang offers equally stunning coastal views (~50,000–80,000 VND). Hoi An Ancient Town charges a heritage ticket (~120,000 VND) for entry to historic houses and museums.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 – April 21 (Hoi An – Culture & Beach)
day_by_day.morning: Purchase a Hoi An Ancient Town heritage ticket (~120,000 VND, includes 5 attraction entries) and spend the morning exploring: the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Chua Cau), the Tan Ky Old House (a 200-year-old merchant home), and the Phuc Kien Assembly Hall with its ornate Chinese architecture. Browse the tailor shops and silk boutiques – Hoi An is famous for custom-made clothing at budget prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND) and cycle 5km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach. Spend the afternoon swimming, relaxing on the sand, and enjoying the laid-back beach atmosphere. An Bang has a great backpacker scene with cheap beach bars and hammock cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ancient Town for the magical lantern-lit evening atmosphere. Visit the colorful Hoi An Night Market on An Hoi Island (free entry). Browse handmade crafts, silk lanterns, and local art. Watch locals and tourists release floating lanterns on the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong – Hoi An's most famous Banh Mi stall (as featured by Anthony Bourdain) (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or Com Ga (Hoi An chicken rice) at a local restaurant near the beach (~60,000–90,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles) at a street stall in the Ancient Town (~50,000–70,000 VND), followed by Che Ba Mau (three-color dessert drink) (~20,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely walkable and bicycle-friendly. The Ancient Town is closed to motorbikes during peak hours. Bargaining is expected at the night market. Consider getting custom clothing made – prices start from ~300,000–500,000 VND for a dress or shirt, ready in 24–48 hours.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Spend a final morning in Hoi An. Visit the local Hoi An Central Market for a vibrant morning scene of fresh produce, spices, and street food. Take a free cooking class demo at the market (~free–50,000 VND for ingredients). Pick up any custom clothing orders from tailors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Da Nang Airport (30km, ~150,000–200,000 VND by taxi or Grab) and take a budget domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Budget airlines like VietJet Air or Bamboo Airways offer tickets from ~500,000–900,000 VND if booked in advance. Arrive in HCMC, take the bus or Grab to the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district and check into a budget hostel (~150,000–250,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Pham Ngu Lao (PNL) backpacker area – the budget travel hub of HCMC. Walk along Bui Vien Walking Street, famous for its neon lights, street bars, and backpacker energy. Grab a cheap Bia Hoi and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: Cao Lau or Banh Mi one last time in Hoi An (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or a meal near Da Nang Airport (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork, egg, and pickled vegetables) – HCMC's iconic dish – at a street stall near Pham Ngu Lao (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights well in advance for the best budget prices. Alternatively, take the overnight sleeper bus from Da Nang/Hoi An to HCMC (~300,000–450,000 VND, ~18–20 hours) to save on accommodation. Da Nang Airport is modern and manageable. HCMC traffic is intense – use Grab for safe and transparent pricing.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23 (Ho Chi Minh City – History & Street Food)
day_by_day.morning: Start with a visit to the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) – one of the most powerful and sobering museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Allow 2 hours. Walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) – the former presidential palace where the Vietnam War officially ended on April 30, 1975, with intact war rooms and vintage helicopters on the roof.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ben Thanh Market – HCMC's most famous market for souvenirs, clothing, and street food (bargain hard – initial prices are often 2–3x the real price). Walk to the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon (currently under renovation but iconic exterior) and the French colonial Central Post Office, designed by Gustave Eiffel – both free to view. Explore the charming Book Street (Duong Sach) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget street food walking tour of District 1 or District 4 (self-guided or organized tours from ~200,000–400,000 VND). District 4, just across the bridge, is known as HCMC's street food paradise. Try multiple dishes from different stalls. End the night with Vietnamese iced coffee and rooftop bar views of the HCMC skyline.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Hu Tieu (Southern-style noodle soup) at a local breakfast stall near your hostel (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Street food crawl at Ben Thanh Market's food stalls (~80,000–120,000 VND for multiple small dishes)
meals.dinner: District 4 street food feast: Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls), and Oc (snails cooked various ways) (~100,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: HCMC moves fast – be aware of motorbike traffic when crossing streets (walk slowly and steadily). The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense – allow time to process. Grab is essential in HCMC. Consider a half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~120km round trip, ~200,000–350,000 VND via budget tour) if time allows.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 – April 24 (Cu Chi Tunnels & Farewell)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning budget group tour to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport and entry, ~1.5 hours each way). Explore the remarkable 250km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the Vietnam War. Crawl through the tunnels (claustrophobic but incredible), see booby traps, underground kitchens, and war-era exhibits. This is one of Vietnam's most unique historical experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Head to the Saigon Botanical Garden and Zoo for a peaceful break (~500 VND – one of the cheapest entry fees in the world). Alternatively, explore the trendy Thao Dien or Bui Thi Xuan areas for hip cafés and street art. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Binh Tay Market in Chinatown (Cho Lon) – better prices than Ben Thanh.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Vietnamese dinner in the city. Stroll along the Nguyen Hue Walking Street – a grand pedestrian boulevard lined with fountains and the iconic City Hall. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Vietnamese culture, food, and history. Head to the airport for departure or rest up at your hostel.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Xoi (sticky rice) grabbed quickly before the morning tour (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Cu Chi or back in HCMC – try Canh Chua Ca (sweet and sour fish soup) and Ca Kho To (caramelized fish in clay pot) (~70,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Farewell feast at a local Quan Nhau (Vietnamese beer garden/eatery) with grilled meats, fresh vegetables, and cold beer (~120,000–180,000 VND) – a perfect final Vietnamese meal

day_by_day.notes: Book Cu Chi Tunnels tour the evening before through your hostel for best prices. There are two sites – Ben Dinh (smaller, more authentic) and Ben Duoc (larger, more touristy) – Ben Dinh is recommended for backpackers. Allow extra time for airport transfer in HCMC – traffic can be heavy, especially during rush hours (7–9 AM, 5–7 PM). Tan Son Nhat Airport is about 30–45 minutes from the city center by Grab (~80,000–120,000 VND).

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter (approximately 45 minutes by taxi or Grab, ~200,000 VND). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter to shake off jet lag. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and surrounding lanes. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake (entrance ~30,000 VND) for a peaceful introduction to Hanoi's culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ta Hien Street ('Beer Street') for the classic Hanoi street food and bia hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) experience. Soak in the buzzing Old Quarter night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Bun cha at Bun Cha Huong Lien (Obama's bun cha spot) — ~60,000–80,000 VND. A perfect first authentic Hanoi meal.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl on Ta Hien and Dinh Liet streets — try banh mi (~25,000 VND), nem ran (fried spring rolls, ~30,000 VND), and finish with egg coffee at Cafe Giang (~25,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab app for reliable and affordable transportation from the airport. Exchange some currency to VND at the airport or an ATM in the Old Quarter. Keep the first day light to adjust to the time zone.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (open Tue–Thu & Sat–Sun mornings, ~8:00–11:00). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Dress modestly. Free to low-cost entry (~40,000 VND for some sections).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (entry ~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums showcasing Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups with outdoor traditional house exhibits. Grab a Grab bike back to the Old Quarter afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Watch a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (~100,000 VND for a 50-minute show) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form. Book tickets in advance.

meals.breakfast: Pho bo (beef pho) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street — ~60,000 VND. Arrive early as it sells out by mid-morning.
meals.lunch: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a local stall near the Ethnology Museum — ~40,000–50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cha ca La Vong restaurant on Cha Ca Street — grilled turmeric fish with dill, a Hanoi specialty (~150,000–180,000 VND per person, mid-range splurge worth it)

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and during October–November for maintenance. Confirm opening times before visiting. Book Water Puppet Show tickets online or at the theater box office earlier in the day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh — depart early by bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station (~80,000–120,000 VND, 2-hour journey). Explore Trang An Landscape Complex by boat (~200,000 VND for a 2.5-hour rowing boat tour through karst caves and rice paddies — a UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb Mua Cave (Dragon Mountain) for a panoramic view over Ninh Binh's stunning landscape (~100,000 VND entry, ~500 steep steps). Visit Bich Dong Pagoda nearby for a serene cave temple experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus or shared minivan. Relax in the Old Quarter with a quiet dinner and an early night to recover.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice) from a street vendor near your hotel — ~20,000–30,000 VND before departing
meals.lunch: Com rang (fried rice) or local set lunch near Trang An — ~60,000–80,000 VND at a riverside restaurant
meals.dinner: Bun bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) at a local Old Quarter restaurant — ~60,000–70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is best visited as a day trip from Hanoi. Rent a bicycle locally (~50,000 VND/day) to get between sites. Wear comfortable shoes — Mua Cave climb is strenuous but rewarding. April weather in Ninh Binh is generally warm and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the overnight train or morning train to Hue (book VN Railways ticket in advance, ~200,000–350,000 VND for hard seat or soft seat, ~13–14 hours) OR take a budget flight (~500,000–800,000 VND with VietJet or Bamboo Airways, 1 hour). Fly for efficiency on a 10-day trip. Depart Hanoi, arrive Hue by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Hue's city center (~300,000–500,000 VND/night). Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and explore the Imperial Citadel of Hue (entry ~200,000 VND) — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River at sunset. Explore Hue's vibrant Dong Ba Market for local snacks and handicrafts.

meals.breakfast: Quick banh mi or xoi at Hanoi airport or hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Bun bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup) at a local eatery near Dong Ba Market — ~50,000–70,000 VND. This is the dish's hometown!
meals.dinner: Com hen (baby clam rice) and banh khoai (crispy Hue pancake) at a street stall near the Perfume River — ~40,000–60,000 VND each

day_by_day.notes: Hue is Vietnam's former imperial capital and a food paradise. Book flights early for the best prices. The Imperial Citadel is large — allocate 2–3 hours. Hue's cuisine is distinct from Hanoi and Saigon — try as many local specialties as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike (~120,000–150,000 VND/day) or join a guided tour to explore Hue's Royal Tombs. Visit Tu Duc Tomb and Khai Dinh Tomb (~150,000 VND each) — elaborate mausoleums set in forested hillsides outside the city. The contrast in architectural styles is fascinating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free entry) — Hue's iconic seven-story pagoda on the banks of the Perfume River. Take a dragon boat ride back to the city center (~150,000–200,000 VND per boat, shareable). Stop at a local lacquerware or conical hat workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hue's night market along Le Loi Street. Enjoy a leisurely dinner featuring the full spectrum of Hue royal cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Banh beo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) at a traditional Hue breakfast spot — ~30,000–40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with street snacks near the Royal Tombs — nem lui (lemongrass pork skewers) wrapped in rice paper ~40,000 VND
meals.dinner: Royal Hue set dinner at Tinh Gia Vien restaurant (~200,000–250,000 VND/person) — a mid-range splurge for an authentic imperial dining experience in a restored garden house

day_by_day.notes: Motorbike rental requires an international driving permit or local license technically, but many tourists rent without issue — use judgment and always wear a helmet. The Royal Tombs are spread out — a motorbike or hired car is most efficient. Combine multiple tombs into one morning.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or train from Hue to Hoi An via the Hai Van Pass (~3.5 hours by tourist bus, ~150,000–200,000 VND). The Hai Van Pass road journey is one of Vietnam's most scenic — consider hiring a motorbike taxi (xe om) or joining a small group motorbike tour over the pass (~400,000–600,000 VND) for a memorable experience. Stop at Lang Co Beach en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town (~350,000–600,000 VND/night). Purchase a Hoi An Ancient Town ticket (~120,000 VND, includes 5 heritage site entries) and explore the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, merchant houses, and Assembly Halls.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the lantern-lit Ancient Town streets at dusk — most magical in the early evening. Browse the night market along the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or banh mi from a Hue street stall before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside shack at Lang Co (~80,000–100,000 VND) if stopping en route
meals.dinner: Cao lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and greens) at Cao Lau Thanh restaurant — ~60,000–80,000 VND. Authentic cao lau uses water from a specific local well — a truly unique dish.

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass motorbike tour is a highlight many backpackers cite as a trip highlight — highly recommended if weather permits. Book a reliable operator in Hue the evening before. Hoi An Ancient Town is pedestrian-only in the evenings — embrace the slow pace.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking class in Hoi An (~500,000–700,000 VND) — most include a market visit to Hoi An Central Market, a boat ride to a herb garden, and hands-on cooking of 4–5 Vietnamese dishes. One of the best cultural experiences in Vietnam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle 5 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a relaxing afternoon swim and beach time. April in Hoi An is warm and generally sunny — ideal beach weather.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ancient Town for the lantern festival atmosphere. Visit a tailor shop if interested in custom-made clothing (Hoi An is famous for fast, affordable tailoring — 24–48 hour turnaround, ~400,000–800,000 VND for a dress or shirt).

meals.breakfast: White rose dumplings (banh bao vac) and fried wontons at a street stall near the market — ~30,000–40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Included in cooking class — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Com ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at Ba Buoi restaurant — a beloved local institution, ~60,000–80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one day in advance — Morning Glory, Red Bridge, and Thuan Tinh Island are all well-regarded options. If ordering from a tailor, do so today or tomorrow to allow enough time for fittings before you leave Hoi An.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or shuttle from Hoi An to Da Nang Airport (~45 minutes, ~50,000–100,000 VND) and fly to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — ~1 hour flight (~400,000–700,000 VND with budget airlines). Check into a mid-range hostel or guesthouse in District 1 or the Backpacker District (Pham Ngu Lao area, ~300,000–600,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum (entry ~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering museum documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Essential cultural context for understanding modern Vietnam. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district — buzzing with street food stalls, bars, and travel agencies. Walk to Ben Thanh Market area for evening street food.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick banh mi (~25,000 VND) near your Hoi An guesthouse before departure
meals.lunch: Hu tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style noodle soup) from a street cart near the museum area — ~50,000–60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Street food at the Ben Thanh Night Market — try banh xeo (sizzling crepe, ~60,000 VND), che (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup, ~20,000 VND), and fresh coconut (~20,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — allow time to process. Photography is permitted. HCMC is significantly larger and faster-paced than Hanoi — use Grab for all transportation. District 1 is the most convenient base for sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~70 km northwest of HCMC). Book a half-day or full-day guided tour (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport) departing around 7:30–8:00 AM. Crawl through the narrow wartime tunnels, see booby traps, and learn about Viet Cong guerrilla tactics — a fascinating and humbling historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Visit the Reunification Palace (entry ~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, preserved exactly as it was on April 30, 1975. Explore the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica and the Central Post Office (French colonial architecture) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker nightlife street. Enjoy live music, street performances, and the electric atmosphere. Try a rooftop bar in District 1 for skyline views (~80,000–120,000 VND for a cocktail).

meals.breakfast: Banh mi op la (egg banh mi) from a street cart near your guesthouse — ~25,000–35,000 VND
meals.lunch: Lunch included or available near Cu Chi Tunnels site (~80,000–100,000 VND for a local set meal)
meals.dinner: Com tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at a local com tam restaurant in District 1 — ~60,000–80,000 VND. This is HCMC's quintessential everyday dish.

day_by_day.notes: Book Cu Chi Tunnels tour the evening before through your guesthouse or a reputable travel agency. Wear comfortable, dark clothing you don't mind getting dusty. The Ben Dinh site (less touristy) is preferable to Ben Duoc. Carry water — it gets hot inside the tunnels.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the vibrant Binh Tay Market in Cholon (Chinatown) — HCMC's largest wholesale market with colorful produce, spices, and goods. Explore the surrounding Cholon district's Chinese temples, including Thien Hau Pagoda (free entry) — dedicated to the goddess of the sea, filled with incense coils and ornate decor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Saigon: Browse Dong Khoi Street for last-minute souvenirs (lacquerware, silk, Vietnamese coffee, pho spice kits). Visit the Fine Arts Museum (~30,000 VND) in a stunning French colonial villa. Enjoy a final Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da, ~25,000–35,000 VND) at a sidewalk cafe and reflect on the journey.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport as needed. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Dim sum breakfast in Cholon at a Chinese-Vietnamese teahouse (~60,000–80,000 VND) — a unique HCMC experience
meals.lunch: Banh mi from the legendary Banh Mi Huynh Hoa on Le Thi Rieng Street — widely considered HCMC's best, ~40,000–50,000 VND. Expect a short queue.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Vietnamese restaurant — try lau (Vietnamese hotpot) shared with fellow travelers (~150,000–200,000 VND/person) or a final bowl of pho at a classic pho shop

day_by_day.notes: Tan Son Nhat Airport is only 7–8 km from District 1 but traffic can be severe — budget 45–60 minutes by Grab during peak hours. Pack any purchased conical hats or fragile items carefully. Vietnam's 10 days will have covered an incredible north-to-south cultural and culinary journey — from Hanoi's Old Quarter to Saigon's streets. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.date: Day 1 – April 15, 2027 (Arrival Day)
day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter, Hanoi (approximately 45 minutes). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter – absorb the sensory overload of silk shops, street vendors, and French colonial architecture at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel rooftop or a nearby rooftop bar overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake. Follow with a curated evening walk around Hoan Kiem Lake and the illuminated Ngoc Son Temple on Jade Island.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit or light snack at airport
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chả Cá Thăng Long – a Hanoi institution serving the legendary turmeric-marinated grilled fish (chả cá) cooked tableside with dill and spring onions. Reserve a private dining room for a premium experience.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup in advance with a premium car service. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Exchange currency or use hotel concierge for VND cash needs.

day_by_day.date: Day 2 – April 16, 2027 (Hanoi Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private guided street food walking tour of the Old Quarter. Visit a traditional bánh mì cart, a pho alley beloved by locals, and a bun oc (snail noodle soup) stall. Stop at a century-old tea house for Vietnamese lotus tea. Explore Dong Xuan Market – Hanoi's oldest and largest covered market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070. Followed by a visit to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology for a world-class cultural immersion into the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. Hire a private art guide to explore the surrounding gallery district.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (book premium front-row seats). Stroll the pedestrianized streets around Hoan Kiem for the vibrant weekend night market atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Street food tour breakfast – authentic pho bo (beef noodle soup) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street, a legendary 70-year-old establishment.
meals.lunch: Bun cha at Bun Cha Huong Lien (the 'Obama Bun Cha' restaurant) – a cultural landmark. Opt for the private dining section.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at La Badiane – French-Vietnamese fusion cuisine in a beautifully restored colonial villa. Tasting menu with wine pairing recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Book Water Puppet Theatre tickets at least 2 days in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the morning food tour. The Museum of Ethnology is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Culture & Hidden Gems)
day_by_day.morning: Private cyclo (rickshaw) tour through the ancient trade streets of the Old Quarter with a local historian guide. Visit the ancient Quan Thanh Temple and stroll around West Lake (Ho Tay) – Hanoi's largest lake. Stop at Tran Quoc Pagoda, the oldest Buddhist pagoda in Hanoi, located on a small island in West Lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the French Quarter – admire the Hanoi Opera House, the Presidential Palace complex, and Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House and Mausoleum (exterior viewing). Visit the Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton') for a sobering and important historical perspective. Afternoon coffee at Café Dinh – a legendary hidden café accessed through a narrow alleyway.
day_by_day.evening: Premium cooking class experience at a renowned Hanoi culinary school – learn to prepare nem cuon (fresh spring rolls), pho broth from scratch, and banh xeo (sizzling crepes). Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) at Banh Cuon Ba Hanh – a beloved Old Quarter breakfast spot.
meals.lunch: Bun bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle bowl) at a curated local restaurant near the French Quarter.
meals.dinner: Your own creations at the cooking class, supplemented by a welcome cocktail and local craft beer tasting.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and the complex has a strict dress code (covered shoulders and knees). Book the cooking class 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – April 18, 2027 (Halong Bay Luxury Cruise – Embarkation)
day_by_day.morning: Hotel checkout and private luxury transfer to Tuan Chau Marina (approximately 2.5 hours from Hanoi). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Red River Delta countryside. Arrive at the marina and board your premium overnight cruise vessel – choose a 5-star boutique junk boat such as Paradise Elegance, Indochine Sails, or Bhaya Classic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Set sail through the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Halong Bay. Kayaking through hidden lagoons and sea caves (Luon Cave or Dark & Bright Cave). Swimming stop at an emerald-water cove. Guided visit to Surprise Cave (Hang Sung Sot) – the largest and most spectacular grotto in Halong Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck as the limestone karsts turn golden. Squid fishing off the stern of the boat under the stars. Private cabin relaxation with in-room amenities.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before departure – Vietnamese egg coffee and banh mi at the hotel's café.
meals.lunch: Welcome seafood lunch aboard the cruise – fresh crab, grilled squid, and Vietnamese salads served as the boat departs.
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course seafood dinner onboard – live lobster, steamed clams, fish in ginger sauce, and local vegetables, paired with Vietnamese wine or premium beer.

day_by_day.notes: Pack a small overnight bag for the cruise – leave larger luggage at the hotel's storage. Bring sunscreen, a light jacket for evenings on the water, and motion sickness tablets if needed. Confirm cruise booking at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19, 2027 (Halong Bay – Return to Hanoi / Depart for Hoi An)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck at sunrise. Explore Vung Vieng Floating Fishing Village by bamboo basket boat – interact with local fishing families. Enjoy a farewell brunch onboard as the cruise returns to Tuan Chau Marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and private transfer back to Hanoi. Catch an afternoon domestic flight from Noi Bai Airport to Da Nang (approximately 1.5 hours). Private luxury transfer from Da Nang Airport to Hoi An Ancient Town (approximately 30 minutes). Check in to a premium Hoi An boutique resort or heritage hotel (e.g., Anantara Hoi An Resort or The Nam Hai).
day_by_day.evening: First evening stroll through Hoi An Ancient Town – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The lantern-lit streets, Japanese Covered Bridge, and riverside are magical at dusk. Browse artisan shops and tailor boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Onboard cruise breakfast – fresh fruit, congee, eggs to order, and Vietnamese iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Farewell brunch onboard – Vietnamese pancakes, spring rolls, and noodle dishes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Morning Glory Restaurant in Hoi An – owned by celebrated chef Trinh Diem Vy, serving elevated Central Vietnamese cuisine in a beautiful heritage building.

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Hanoi to Da Nang in advance. Coordinate hotel check-in time with resort as arrival may be late afternoon. Hoi An Ancient Town is best explored on foot – leave vehicles at the perimeter.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20, 2027 (Hoi An Culture & Craft Immersion)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided bicycle tour through the rice paddies and villages surrounding Hoi An. Visit Tra Que Vegetable Village – a 400-year-old organic farming community. Participate in a farm-to-table gardening experience: plant, harvest, and prepare your own herbs. Visit a traditional lantern-making workshop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ancient Town on foot with a private cultural guide: Japanese Covered Bridge (Cau Nhat Ban), Tan Ky Old House, Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and the vibrant Central Market. Visit a bespoke tailor for a fitting – Hoi An is world-renowned for custom clothing made within 24–48 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride along the Thu Bon River on a traditional wooden sampan, releasing flower lanterns onto the water. Attend a traditional Hoi An folk music and dance performance at the Hoi An Impression Theme Park or a heritage house.

meals.breakfast: Cao lau (Hoi An's iconic thick noodle dish, made with water from a specific ancient well) at a riverside café.
meals.lunch: White Rose dumplings (banh bao vac) and fried wontons at White Rose Restaurant – the only place authorized to make this Hoi An specialty.
meals.dinner: The Deck Restaurant at Anantara Hoi An – riverside fine dining with contemporary Vietnamese cuisine and an extensive cocktail list.

day_by_day.notes: Tailor visit should happen early in the day to allow time for fittings and alterations before departure. Bring a reference photo for any custom clothing. Lantern release is best done after 18:00 when the river is atmospheric.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 – April 21, 2027 (My Son Sanctuary & Hoi An Culinary Arts)
day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise tour to My Son Sanctuary – the ancient Cham Hindu temple complex dating from the 4th–14th centuries, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Arrive before the crowds for a serene, atmospheric experience among the jungle-draped ruins. A private guide will explain the Cham civilization's history and artistry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An for a premium hands-on cooking class at the Red Bridge Cooking School – located on a scenic riverfront property. Take a market tour, then cook a full Vietnamese feast including Hoi An specialties. Collect your tailored clothing from the tailor.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at leisure – explore the night market along Nguyen Hoang Street. Browse handmade silk lanterns, lacquerware, and local art. Enjoy a traditional Vietnamese herbal foot massage and spa treatment at a premium wellness center.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi Phuong – widely considered the best bánh mì in Vietnam (and the world, according to Anthony Bourdain). Queue is worth it.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared at Red Bridge Cooking School as your lunch.
meals.dinner: Mango Rooms Restaurant – a beloved Hoi An institution with creative Vietnamese fusion dishes in a colorful riverside setting.

day_by_day.notes: My Son is approximately 40km from Hoi An – depart by 06:00 for sunrise. The ruins can be hot and exposed; bring a hat and water. Red Bridge Cooking School requires advance booking.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22, 2027 (An Bang Beach & Depart for Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure – spend a relaxing few hours at An Bang Beach, one of Vietnam's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches, just 5km from Hoi An. Lounge in a premium beach club (Soul Kitchen or An Bang Beach Club) with a beachside breakfast and swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Da Nang Airport. Domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) – approximately 1.5 hours. Private luxury transfer to your hotel in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City (e.g., Park Hyatt Saigon, The Reverie Saigon, or Hotel des Arts Saigon). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: First evening exploration of Ho Chi Minh City – walk through the historic center: Dong Khoi Street, the Saigon Opera House, Notre-Dame Cathedral (exterior), and the Central Post Office. Rooftop cocktails at the Chill Skybar (49th floor of AB Tower) for panoramic city views at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Beachside breakfast at An Bang Beach Club – fresh tropical fruit, Vietnamese iced coffee, and egg dishes.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or onboard.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Deck Saigon – an iconic riverside restaurant on the banks of the Saigon River in District 2, serving modern Vietnamese cuisine in a stunning setting.

day_by_day.notes: Check Da Nang–HCMC flight times carefully and book in advance. Ho Chi Minh City traffic can be intense – allow extra time for airport transfers. District 1 is the ideal base for exploring the city.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City – History, Culture & Street Food)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided historical tour: Reunification Palace (Independence Palace) – walk through the iconic building that marked the end of the Vietnam War. Visit the War Remnants Museum – one of the most visited museums in Southeast Asia, offering a powerful and moving account of the Vietnam War.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Ben Thanh Market area and the surrounding street food alleys. Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda – one of Saigon's most atmospheric temples, filled with incense smoke and intricate Taoist iconography. Explore the hip Bui Vien Street area and the artsy District 3 café scene.
day_by_day.evening: Premium street food tour of District 1 and District 4 with a private local food guide – taste banh xeo (sizzling crepe), goi cuon (fresh spring rolls), com tam (broken rice with grilled pork), and che (sweet dessert soup). End at a rooftop bar for nightcaps.

meals.breakfast: Pho at Pho Le – a legendary HCMC pho institution in District 5 (Cholon), famous for its rich, clear broth.
meals.lunch: Bun bo Hue (spicy Central Vietnamese beef noodle soup) at a curated local restaurant in District 3.
meals.dinner: Street food progressive dinner tour – multiple stops across Districts 1 and 4, guided by a premium food tour operator (Saigon Street Eats or XO Tours).

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum contains graphic imagery – be mentally prepared. Hire a licensed private guide for the Reunification Palace for the full historical context. Dress modestly for temple visits.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 – April 24, 2027 (Mekong Delta Day Trip & Farewell)
day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium private tour to the Mekong Delta – depart early by private vehicle to My Tho or Ben Tre (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Board a private wooden boat and cruise through the intricate network of canals, past floating markets, coconut palm forests, and river islands. Visit a coconut candy workshop, a traditional rice paper factory, and a honey bee farm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a floating market by sampan boat (Cai Rang or Phung Hiep). Cycle through riverside villages on rented bicycles. Enjoy a traditional Mekong lunch on a river island. Return to Ho Chi Minh City in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premium Saigon restaurant. Final stroll along Nguyen Hue Walking Street – Ho Chi Minh City's most iconic pedestrian boulevard, lined with fountains and the stunning City Hall. Last-minute souvenir shopping at premium boutiques on Dong Khoi Street.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – a lavish spread at the Park Hyatt or Reverie Saigon's restaurant.
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong Delta lunch on a river island – elephant ear fish (ca tai tuong) wrapped in rice paper with herbs, fresh coconut juice, and river shrimp.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Noir – Dining in the Dark (a unique sensory experience) or at Cuc Gach Quan, a charming restored villa restaurant serving rustic Vietnamese home cooking beloved by locals and travelers alike.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for the Mekong Delta by 07:30 to maximize time on the water. Book the farewell dinner restaurant in advance. If departing Vietnam on April 25, confirm airport transfer time with hotel concierge and allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Consider a premium airport lounge pass for the final departure.
